Step 1 places a single 2x2 plate. It is the first piece of the model, so it rests on nothing.
The plate looks dark grey in the booklet image. The only 2x2 plate in the parts list is Black (lego-3022), so I used that.
Step 2: a 2x3 plate is added and slides onto the 2x2 plate (b1) so they overlap. The drawing is ambiguous about the overlap, so I recorded that the 2x3 clutches b1.
Step 3: a 1x6 plate sits on top of the plates below it. It is listed as resting on both b2 and b1, since it appears to span both. I could not check the exact overlap.
Colours are guessed from the grey-toned drawings. The 2x3 plate, 1x6 plate and 2x2 plate are all black in the parts list.
Step 4 adds a 1x3 plate turned at a right angle to the 1x6 plate, forming an L shape. I recorded that it clutches the end of the 1x6 plate (b3).
Colour is assumed black (lego-3623 Black) because the drawing is grey-toned.

Step 5: the 2x6 plate with 4 studs on its side is lowered onto the top of the assembly. It is shown with the side studs facing outward. I recorded it as resting on b2, b3 and b4, based on my reading of the top view.

Step 6: the 4x6 plate is added in front of and to the left of the assembly. In the drawing it looks level with the bottom of the assembly. I read it as sitting beneath the overlapping plates and clutching their undersides, so I gave it rests_on []. The exact overlap is unclear.
Colours are assumed black because the drawings are grey-toned.
Step 7: a 2x2 corner plate is placed in the joint between the 4x6 plate (b6) and the upper assembly. I recorded it as resting on b6 and b2.
Step 8: a 2x2 plate is pushed onto the studs at the same joint, bridging the 4x6 plate and the upper assembly. The arrows are small, so which pieces it clutches is a best estimate: b6, b3 and b7.
Colours are assumed black because the drawings are grey-toned. The 2x2 corner plate is also available in white, but the drawing shows dark.
Step 9: a 2x6 plate is laid over the upper assembly, bridging the plates below. Which pieces it clutches is a best estimate: b5, b8 and b7.
Step 10: a green 1x2 plate is placed at the left end of the 2x6 plate (b9). I recorded it as resting on b9, but it may overhang the edge slightly.
Colours of the black parts are assumed from the grey-toned drawings. The 1x2 plate is clearly green in the drawing.

Step 11: a 2x3 plate is pushed in at the left side, bridging the 4x6 plate (b6) and the plates of the upper assembly. The arrows are small, so the set of pieces it clutches (b6, b9, b8) is a best estimate.
Step 12: a 2x6 plate is laid across the left part of the base. I recorded it as resting on b6, b11 and b9. This is a best estimate from the isometric view.
Colours are assumed black because the drawings are grey-toned.

Step 13: a 2x2 plate is pushed in from the front, at the lowest layer, so its studs go up into the plates above it (b12/b6). I recorded rests_on [] because nothing is beneath it. The drawing does not show the join clearly.
Step 14: a 1x3 plate is added at the left end of the base. I recorded it as resting on the 2x2 plate (b13), which is a guess.
Colours are assumed black because the drawings are grey-toned.

Step 15 adds a 2x10 plate that extends the base to the left, sticking out like a long arm. It sits at the lowest layer and its right end tucks under the left end of the existing plates (around b13/b14), so its studs clutch their undersides. I recorded rests_on [] since nothing is beneath it. The exact overlap is a guess.
Colour is assumed black (lego-3832 Black) because the drawing is grey-toned. The set also has a green 2x10, but the drawing does not show green here.
The 1:1 inset shows the actual size of the 2x10 plate.

Step 16 adds a green 2x6 plate with 4 side studs on top of the long 2x10 plate, near where it meets the main body. The side studs face front, as shown in the inset. I recorded it as resting on b15 and b14, which is a best estimate.
Step 17 adds the green 2x10 plate on top of the long 2x10 base arm (b15) and the green 2x6 plate (b16). I recorded it as resting on both, which is a best estimate from the isometric view.
Step 18 adds four green 1x2 plates in a row along the front edge of the long base arm (b15). They fill the strip of black plate left uncovered beside the green 2x10 (b17).
I recorded the first three as resting on b15 only. The fourth is the one nearest the main body, so I also listed b14 as a best estimate. The drawing is too small to show the exact positions.
Step 19 adds a black 1x2 plate on the exposed left end of the long base arm (b15), next to the green plates.

The green 1x2 plates of steps 10 and 18 look to have been deducted from the black 1x2 count in the remaining-parts list (black went 14 to 9, green stayed at 14). I kept the colours I see in the drawings: green in steps 10 and 18, black here.

Step 20 adds a black 2x6 plate with 4 side studs onto the left end of the long base arm. The inset shows the side studs facing front. I recorded it as resting on b15 and b22, which is a best estimate.
Step 21 adds a white 2x2 corner plate at the left end of the base. I recorded it as resting on b23 and b22, which is a best estimate from the isometric view.
Step 22 adds a black 2x2 corner plate at the left front end of the base. The arrows show it sliding in towards the left end. I recorded it as resting on b15, which is a best estimate.

Step 23 adds a black 1x10 plate that extends from the left front end of the base as a long thin arm. I recorded it as clutching the black corner plate (b25) and the end of b15. The overlap is a best estimate.

Step 24 adds a black 2x3 plate pushed up from below onto the underside of the long 1x10 plate (b26), near its left end. The arrows point up, so the new plate sits underneath. I recorded rests_on [] since nothing is beneath it, and its studs clutch the bottom of b26.
Step 25 adds a 2x2 corner plate pushed up from below onto the underside of the far left end of the 1x10 plate (b26). I recorded rests_on [] since nothing is beneath it.
The colour is black, because it is drawn dark. That is also the third black corner plate in the set, matching the 3 black and 3 white corner plates in the parts list.

Step 26 adds a black 2x6 plate with 4 side studs, lowered onto the long left arm. The side studs face front, as in the inset. I recorded it as resting on b26 and b25, which is a best estimate from the arrows.

Step 27 adds a black 1x3 plate on the left arm, next to the 2x6 plate with side studs (b29). The drawing has no arrows, so its exact position is a best estimate. I recorded it as resting on b29 and b26.
Step 28 adds a black 2x2 plate and a dark tan 1x2 plate with a handle on one end. There are no arrows, so the positions are best estimates.
I read the 2x2 plate as sitting on the left arm over b29 and b30. The tan handle plate is on the left arm next to the white corner plate (b24) and rests on b26 and b30.
The drawing is too small to show the exact positions.
Step 29 adds three small pieces to the left arm: a green 1x2 plate, a dark tan 1x2 plate with a handle, and a white 2x2 corner plate. They sit near the far left end, beside the pieces from step 28.
The drawing has no arrows and is small, so the positions and what each piece rests on (b29, b31) are best estimates.
Step 30 flips the model upside down (rotate icon) and attaches a sub-assembly to its underside along the front edge.

Sub-step 1: the printed 'Chicago' 1x8 tile goes onto a 1x2 plate. Sub-step 2: the same tile goes onto a 1x6 plate. Together the 1x6 and 1x2 plates (6+2 = 8 studs) sit side by side under the 1x8 tile, so I recorded the tile as resting on both.
The plates' studs point toward the flipped model's underside. I recorded them as joined to the long base arm (b15) with other_joins. Which pieces they actually clutch is a best estimate.

The parts callout also shows a 1x4 black tile with groove. The drawing does not show where it goes, so I recorded it with rests_on [] and no join. It is probably placed on the underside in a later step.
Step 31 adds two black 1x8 tiles, drawn at 1:1 size in the inset. Tiles have no studs, so they can only go on the side studs of the 2x6 plates that have 4 studs on one long side.

One tile covers the exposed side studs along the front, to the right of the 'Chicago' tile, next to b16. The other covers side studs along the back edge, next to b5. Each tile is joined sideways, so I recorded them as other_joins and gave rests_on [].
The exact plates they attach to, and which plate goes to which tile, are best estimates.
Step 32 adds one 1x4 tile and seven 2x2 corner tiles, all light bluish gray, to cover the studs of the main body (the right-hand part of the base).
The parts callout shows the 1x4 tile once and the corner tiles 7 times. The tiles interlock like a jigsaw over the original base plates (b5, b9, b11, b12, b8), which is a best estimate.
The drawing is small, so the exact position of each tile, and which plates each rests on, are guesses.

Step 33 uses the parts in the callout. Top row: a clip tile, a turntable top, 4 trans-light-blue 1x4 tiles, and a turntable base. Bottom row: a 1x4 tile, 3 small 1x1 plates, a 1x2 tile, and 2 corner tiles.
The turntable top is first pressed onto the turntable base in the inset, so I recorded it as a hinge join (rotates). The base goes on the studs of the main body.
The four trans-light-blue tiles cover the left part of the green 2x10 plate (b17). The remaining light-grey tiles and plates fill gaps in the tile covering at the right end.
The small 1x1 pieces ('3x') look like 1x1 plates in light bluish gray, so I used lego-3024.
The positions and the pieces each one rests on are best estimates from a small isometric drawing.

Step 34 covers most of the left part of the base with light-bluish-gray pieces: one 2x2 jumper plate, eight 1x2 jumper plates, two 1x1 plates, three 1x2 tiles, three corner tiles and one clip tile. The far-left strip is left with exposed black studs.
The jumper plates fill the left arm, and the tiles and corner tiles cover over them. The drawing is small, so the piece positions and what each rests on are best estimates.
The remaining-parts counts decrement oddly (not in step with colours), so I took each colour from the drawings, not from the list.
Step 35 adds three 1x4 tiles and two 1x2 tiles (light bluish gray) over the left part of the base. It also adds a dark 2x2 plate on the far-left exposed studs.
The 2x2 plate shows its studs, so it is not a tile. The only 2x2 plate in the remaining parts is black (lego-3022), so I used that.
Exact positions and what each piece rests on are best estimates from the small isometric drawing.
Page 61 starts a new sub-model: the red tower (Big Red) shown in the top picture. It is built separately and joined to the base later.
Step 36: the first piece is a light grey 2x2 plate with two studs on the side and two raised (lego-99206). It is the first piece of this sub-model, so rests_on is [].
Step 37: two green 1x2 plates are stacked on the raised studs of that plate.
Step 38: a yellow 1x2 brick goes on the remaining studs, next to the green stack. Which studs it clutches is a best estimate, so I recorded it as resting on b88.

Step 39 (built 2x): each red 1x2-2x4 bracket gets four red grille tiles on its tall face, 8 tiles in total. The two finished brackets are then fitted on either side of the stack from steps 36-38. I recorded this as joins to b88, because the fit is sideways. Which studs they clutch is a best estimate.

Step 40: a second small module is built. A light grey 2x2 plate (lego-99206) gets a yellow 1x2 brick, and two green 1x2 plates are stacked, as in steps 36-38. The module sits on top of the first stack, so I recorded b102 as resting on b90 and b91.
Positions are best estimates from the small isometric drawings.

Step 41 (built 2x): each red bracket gets a red 1x4 tile on the lower row of its face studs and two red grille tiles on the upper row. The two finished brackets then fit on either side of the second module (b102), the same way as in step 39.
Step 42: a third module is built, a light grey 2x2 plate (lego-99206) with a yellow 1x2 brick and two stacked green 1x2 plates. It sits on top of the second module, so b114 rests on b105 and b103.
Positions are best estimates from the small isometric drawings.
Step 43 (built 2x): two red brackets, each with four red grille tiles on its face, as in step 39. They are fitted on either side of the third module (b114).
Step 44: a fourth module is built, a light grey 2x2 plate (lego-99206) with a yellow 1x2 brick and two stacked green 1x2 plates. It sits on top of the third module, so b128 rests on b117 and b115.
Positions are best estimates from the small isometric drawings.
Step 45 (built 2x): two red brackets, each with a red 1x4 tile on the lower row and two red grille tiles on the upper row. They are fitted on either side of the fourth module (b128), as in step 41.
Positions are best estimates from the small isometric drawing.
Step 46 is built 2x. Each copy is a black 2x8 plate covered by six red grille tiles and two plain red 1x2 tiles with groove (6 x 2 + 2 x 2 = 16 studs). The two plain red tiles sit at the ends.
Both finished panels are set aside here. The page does not show where they attach, so they have no joins to the tower yet.
The tile arrangement is read from the isometric drawings. The red 1x2 tiles are lego-3069b; the long thin red tiles are the lego-2412b grille tiles.

Step 46 (continued): the two roof panels built on the previous page are attached to the top of the red tower, one along each long edge, with the four red studs of the top brackets left showing in the middle. The drawing is small, so I recorded the panels as joined to the top brackets (b132 and b133) with other_joins. The exact join is a best estimate.
Step 47: a dark bluish gray 2x2 tile with groove (lego-3068b) is placed on the four exposed red studs at the top of the tower. It rests on the two top brackets, b132 and b133.
Step 48 turns the base right way up (rotate icon) and presses the finished red tower (Big Red) onto the studs at the right end of the base. No new pieces are added.

The tower's bottom plate (b88, the first piece of the tower) clutches the base. I recorded this with other_joins to b44 and b45, because b88 was placed earlier with rests_on []. Which base pieces carry the exposed studs is a best estimate.
Step 49 adds two olive green round 1x1 tiles and a Technic ball joint (the silver Cloud Gate bean) on single studs in front of the red tower.

I assumed they sit on the three 1x1 plates (b58, b59, b60) that stand up from the tile covering in step 33. Those plates look black in these drawings, although I recorded them as light bluish gray in step 33. The positions are best estimates.
The ball joint rests on a stud through its axle-hole. Its ball end points up.
Page 70 starts a new sub-model: the Willis Tower, built from a black 3x3 plate base with trans-brown plates.
Step 50: the 3x3 plate is the first piece of the sub-model, so rests_on is [].
Step 51: four trans-brown 1x2 plates are placed around the center stud of the 3x3 plate in a pinwheel.
Step 52: the assembly is flipped over (rotate icon). No pieces are added.
Step 53: one more trans-brown 1x2 plate is placed on the pinwheel ring, near the back edge. I recorded it as resting on b163 and b164, which is a best estimate.
Step 54: two trans-brown 1x2 plates are added to the top of the pinwheel.

Step 55: a small sideways cylinder is built on a black 1x1 plate with clip (lego-4081b). Two round pieces and two round trans-brown tiles make up the cylinder, which is then fitted onto the right side of the model. The drawing is small, so exactly how the round pieces hold together, and which are lego-85861 and which are tiles, is a best estimate.
Step 56: one trans-brown 1x1 plate is added on top of the pinwheel.
Step 57: the model is turned over (rotate icon). No piece is added.
All positions and the pieces each one rests on are best estimates from the small drawings.
Step 58 presses the finished trans-brown sub-assembly from steps 50-57 onto the nine exposed studs at the right end of the base, beside the red tower and the silver bean. No new pieces are added.
I recorded this with other_joins, because b162 was placed earlier with rests_on []. Which base plates carry those studs (b9, b11, b12) is a best estimate.

Step 59 is built 5x. Each layer is a black 3x3 plate with four trans-brown 1x2 plates in a pinwheel around the center stud. The five layers are stacked one on top of the other on the Willis Tower sub-assembly from steps 50-57.
The first layer plate rests on the top pieces of the existing pinwheel (b167, b168, b169). Each following layer plate rests on the four 1x2 plates of the layer below.
The 3x3 plates look dark grey in the drawings, so I used the Black lego-11212. The drawing is small, so the exact stack contacts are best estimates.
Step 60 caps the stack with a 3x3 plate on top of the top layer's four 1x2 plates (b197-b200).
The plate looks dark grey in the drawing, so I used the Black lego-11212.
Steps 61-63 continue the Willis Tower stack. The callout at the top of the page shows the existing stack taken off the model.
Step 61: another black 3x3 plate goes on top of the stack's top plate (b201). I recorded it as resting on b201, which is a best estimate, as it may instead be the base of a second section.
Step 62: four trans-brown 1x2 plates are placed around the center stud in a pinwheel.
Step 63 (built 3x): three more layers, each a black 3x3 plate with four trans-brown 1x2 plates in a pinwheel, are stacked on top. The finished taller stack is shown at the bottom of the page.
The 3x3 plates look dark grey in the drawings, so I used Black lego-11212.

Step 64 fills the top layer of the stack with dark bluish gray pieces: two 1x2 plates, two 1x1 tiles and one 1x3 plate (2+2+2+1+... = 9 cells of a 3x3 top). This forms a flat-looking top over the last pinwheel layer.
The colours match the parts list (Dark Bluish Gray lego-3023, lego-3070b and lego-3623), so I used Dark Bluish Gray, not black.
The exact layout and which of the pinwheel plates each piece rests on are best estimates.
Step 65 presses the taller stack built in steps 61-64 onto the Willis Tower stack on the model. No new pieces are added.
I had already recorded the bottom plate of that stack (b202) as resting on the top plate b201 in step 61, so there is no new connection to add.

Step 66 adds two trans-brown 1x2 plates and two trans-brown 1x1 plates on the studs at the top of the Willis Tower. There are 7 free studs there (from the dark gray 1x3 plate and two 1x2 plates in step 64), and these four pieces cover 6 of them.
Their exact positions and what each rests on are best estimates from the small drawing.
Step 67 adds two dark bluish gray 1x2 plates and one dark bluish gray 1x3 plate on top of the pieces added in step 66. They form the next flat layer of the Willis Tower.
The colours match the parts list, which still holds Dark Bluish Gray lego-3023 and lego-3623. The positions and what each rests on are best estimates.
Step 68 repeats step 66: two trans-brown 1x2 plates and two trans-brown 1x1 plates go on the dark bluish gray layer from step 67.
Their exact positions and what each rests on are best estimates.
Step 69 repeats step 67: two grey 1x2 plates and a grey 1x3 plate go on top of the trans-brown pieces from step 68.

I used Dark Bluish Gray, as in step 64 and step 67. The parts list holds only 3 Dark Bluish Gray 1x2 plates and 1 Dark Bluish Gray 1x3 plate, which is fewer than steps 64, 67 and 69 need. So some of these greys are probably another colour (for example trans-brown or black). I cannot tell from the grey-toned drawings.
Positions and what each rests on are best estimates.
Step 70 repeats step 68: two trans-brown 1x2 plates and two trans-brown 1x1 plates go on the grey layer from step 69.
Their exact positions and what each rests on are best estimates.
Step 71 repeats steps 67 and 69: two grey 1x2 plates and one 1x3 plate go on top of the trans-brown pieces from step 70.

Colours are uncertain. The remaining-parts list drops one Black 1x3 plate (lego-3623) at steps 67, 69 and 71, so the 1x3 plates in those steps are probably Black, not the Dark Bluish Gray I recorded for b233 and b240. I used Black here. The 1x2 plates are recorded as Dark Bluish Gray, but the parts list only holds 3, so some of the earlier ones are probably another colour.
Positions and what each rests on are best estimates.
Step 72 adds two 1x2 plates, two 1x1 tiles with groove and one 1x3 plate to the top of the Willis Tower. This makes a flat layer like step 64.
Colours are guesses from the grey-toned drawing. The 1x3 plate looks light, so I used White (the parts list has 4 White lego-3623). The 1x2 plates are Trans-Brown and the tiles Dark Bluish Gray.
Positions and what each rests on are best estimates.

Step 73 is built 5x as a new smaller upper section of the Willis Tower. Each layer is a black 3x3 cross plate, one trans-brown 1x2 plate and three trans-brown 1x1 plates. The five layers are stacked into a narrower tower and then pressed onto the top of the main stack (shown on the right of the page).
The first cross plate rests on the top pieces from step 72 (b248-b252). Each following cross plate rests on the four plates of the layer below.
The cross plates look dark grey, so I used Black lego-15397. Which cross-plate cells each small plate fills is a best estimate.

Step 74 builds a cap for the narrow upper section: a black 3x3 cross plate with one 1x2 plate and three 1x1 tiles with groove on top. The cap is then pressed onto the top of the upper section from step 73.

I recorded the cap as resting on the four small plates of the top layer (b274-b277). The colours of the grey parts are guesses; the parts list holds Dark Bluish Gray lego-3023 and lego-3070b, so I used those.
Step 75 stacks nine 1x2 plates into a narrow mast (3 dark, 2 medium, 4 lighter, as in the callout). The mast is then pressed onto the free studs of the 1x2 plate (b279) on the cap from step 74.
The drawing shows the stack built from the bottom up in four sub-steps, adding plates two at a time. I recorded the lighter plates at the bottom and the dark ones on top.
Colours are guesses. The parts list holds only 5 Trans-Brown and 3 Dark Bluish Gray 1x2 plates, which is one fewer than the 9 needed, so one of the colours may differ.
Step 76 puts a white round 1x1 plate with open stud (lego-85861) on a free stud at the top of the mast (b291).
The drawing shows a small white round piece, and the parts list has two white lego-85861, so I used that.
Step 77 adds the two white antennas of the Willis Tower, one on the round plate b292 and one on the neighbouring free stud of the mast top (b291).
Step 78 is built 4x: the four bridge houses. Each is a tan 1x1 plate, a tan round 1x1 plate with solid stud on it, and a tan pyramid slope on top.

The four houses are placed on the base around the trans-blue tiled river area (two at each end, one pair near the main tower). I recorded them as resting on the green plate b17, but which base studs they use is a best estimate.
Step 79 is built 2x: each bridge leaf is a dark tan 1x2 plate with handle on one end, topped with a light bluish gray 1x2 tile with groove.

The two leaves are then stood upright beside the bridge houses on either side of the blue-tiled river area. The drawing does not make clear how they hold. I recorded each as joined to the green plate b17, which is a best estimate, and gave rests_on [] for the handle plates.
Page 92 starts a new sub-model: the white Wrigley Building (shown in the top callout).
Step 80: two white 1x3 plates are stacked. The first is the first piece of the sub-model, so rests_on is [].
Step 81: a white 1x1 brick with a stud on one side goes on the end stud of the top plate, and a white 1x2 brick with 2 studs on one side goes on the other two studs.
Step 82: a white 1x3 plate goes on top of those two bricks.
Step 83: another white 1x3 plate goes on top of the previous plate b315.
Step 84: a white 1x2 brick with 2 studs on one side and a white 1x1 brick with a stud on one side go on top of that plate. The drawing shows the 1x2 brick already seated and the 1x1 brick arriving.

Step 85 (2x): two white 1x4 plates are pushed sideways onto the side studs of the bricks, one plate on the 1x2 brick pair and one on the 1x1 brick pair. They are joined sideways, so I used other_joins and gave rests_on [].
Which side studs each 1x4 plate takes is a best estimate.
Step 86 (2x): two white 1x2-1x2 brackets are pressed sideways onto the side studs of the right face of the block.
Step 87: a white 1x4 plate is pressed sideways onto the side studs of the left face of the block.
Step 88: four white window slope bricks (lego-61409) are placed on the outward studs of the two front 1x4 plates (b319 and b320). Two white grille tiles are placed on the left 1x4 plate (b323).
Step 89: two white grille tiles go on the outward studs of the two right-hand brackets.
All these joins are sideways, so they are recorded as other_joins and rests_on is []. Which block pieces the brackets and left plate clip onto is a best estimate.
Step 90: a white 2x2 corner plate and a white 1x1 plate are put on the top studs of the Wrigley Building block. I recorded both as resting on b317 and b318, a best estimate.
Step 91: another white 1x1 plate goes on the corner plate.
Step 92: a white 1x1 brick with studs on 4 sides is added on top of those plates.

Step 93: a round piece goes on the top stud of the 1x1 brick, and a white lipstick pole (lego-93094) is pushed into it, forming the spire. I used a white round plate with open stud (lego-85861) so the pole can fit in it. The parts list may be short of that piece, since my earlier uses of lego-85861 (steps 55 and 76) were also guesses.
Positions and what each rests on are best estimates.
Step 94 presses the finished white Wrigley Building onto the exposed black studs on the left part of the base. No new pieces are added.

The bottom plate of the building (b311) clutches the studs. Which base plate carries those studs is a best estimate, so I recorded it as a join to b87. The earlier colour guesses for those base studs may be off.

Page 97 starts a new sub-model: the John Hancock Center tower, a slender yellow column (top callout). Step 95 shows 5 sub-steps. The parts callout lists more parts than the 5 sub-steps show: the two black 1x8 tiles, the two round quarter tiles, the 1x2 yellow brick, a third yellow 1x1 brick and a third 4-side-stud brick.
